facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s
history of coronary artery bypass surgery
ejection fraction of 25%
biventricular pacemaker placement
dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration
sinus activity at 72 beats/min
normal PR interval
QRS duration of 160 milliseconds
ST segment depression >1mm in V2 and V3
new discordant ST elevation of 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF
Initial troponin (2 hours after symptom onset): Negative
thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft proximal to circumflex anastomosis

concepts.why: The patient presents with dull chest pain, ST segment depression, and new discordant ST elevation, which are indicative of acute coronary syndrome, and cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of a saphenous vein graft.
The patient's ECG changes and thrombotic occlusion of a saphenous vein graft suggest myocardial infarction, although the initial troponin was negative.
The patient has a history of biventricular pacemaker placement and an ejection fraction of 25%, indicating cardiac failure.
The patient's history of coronary artery bypass surgery, low ejection fraction, and thrombotic occlusion of a saphenous vein graft suggest ischemic cardiomyopathy.
The patient presents with chest pain and ECG changes, but the initial troponin was negative, which could indicate unstable angina.
Cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of a saphenous vein graft, which is a type of graft occlusion.
The negative initial troponin level does not rule out myocardial infarction, and the ECG changes and clinical presentation are consistent with non-ST elevation myocardial infarction.
